questions.q: What does FIRST_VALUE(Name) OVER (PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC) return?
options: The Name of the first row in each partition's window, ordered by ListPrice DESC
The Name of the current row only
The average ListPrice for each color
The Name of the last row in each partition
questions.explain: FIRST_VALUE returns the first value in the window frame, according to the ORDER BY — here, the most expensive product name per color.

questions.q: With the default frame, why does LAST_VALUE(Name) OVER (PARTITION BY Color ORDER BY ListPrice DESC) usually just return the current row's own name?
options: The default frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, so the 'last' visible row is always the current row
LAST_VALUE is broken and should never be used
PARTITION BY disables LAST_VALUE entirely
ORDER BY DESC always breaks LAST_VALUE
questions.explain: The default frame only includes rows up to and including the current row, so from LAST_VALUE's point of view, the current row IS the last one it can see.

questions.q: What frame clause fixes LAST_VALUE so it returns the true last value of the whole partition?
options: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW
PARTITION BY ALL
ORDER BY DESC alone, with no frame needed
questions.explain: This explicit frame tells SQL Server the window is the entire partition, before and after the current row, so LAST_VALUE sees the real last row.

questions.q: Why doesn't FIRST_VALUE suffer from the same default-frame problem as LAST_VALUE?
options: The first row of the partition is always included in the default 'start of partition up to current row' frame
FIRST_VALUE doesn't use OVER() the way LAST_VALUE does
FIRST_VALUE automatically applies ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
FIRST_VALUE can only be used without PARTITION BY
questions.explain: The default frame always starts at the beginning of the partition, so the true first value is always within reach — unlike the true last value, which usually isn't.

questions.q: What is the default frame SQL Server applies when ORDER BY is used inside OVER() with no explicit frame?
options: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
No frame is applied unless PARTITION BY is also present
questions.explain: This default frame is the root cause of the classic LAST_VALUE mistake — it only ever sees up to the current row.
